title: Obsidian Attachmenter
subtitle: Obsidian Attachment Management Plugin
description: An Obsidian plugin that gives attachments per-note folders, downloads remote images and checks paths. For people whose notes have more images than notes.
longDescription: A comprehensive Obsidian plugin designed to streamline attachment management. It enforces a per-note attachment folder structure, keeping your vault organized. Key capabilities include automatically moving pasted images to the correct folder, downloading remote images (including from Canvas) to local storage, and providing tools to check and repair broken attachment paths or clean up empty folders. It supports multiple languages and integrates seamlessly with Obsidian's file explorer.
challenges: Integrating with Obsidian's internal link management
Supporting both Markdown and Canvas files
solutions: Used Obsidian's vault events to track changes
Developed custom handlers for Canvas nodes
why: I wanted one attachment folder per note, right next to it, so moving or archiving a note takes its pictures along. Remote images should become local files rather than links you hope still work, and an existing vault needed tools to get into line.
gains: Pasted images stop arriving as 'Pasted image …' files: each one is renamed after its note and filed beside it. File Explorer also marks which notes still lean on remote images, and one click saves them locally.

lessons: While enabled, it borrows one Obsidian setting: newLinkFormat becomes relative unless it is already relative or shortest, and is put back on unload.
Renaming a single attachment means reading every .md and .canvas file in the vault, just to update the links to it.
